item.title: Fixing Chrome Crashes and DevToolsActivePort Errors with Selenium WebDriver
item.description:
“Fixing Chrome Crashes and DevToolsActivePort Errors with Selenium WebDriver”

Several factors can contribute to this issue, including an improperly installed Chrome browser, incorrect ChromeDriver versions, permission issues, or conflicts within your execution environment. Below, we explore various solutions and code adjustments to help you overcome these common roadblocks.

Understanding the Error

The core of this error lies in ChromeDriver’s inability to communicate with the Chrome browser process. The DevToolsActivePort file doesn't exist message specifically points to a failure in establishing the necessary connection for debugging and control. The system assumes Chrome has crashed when this communication channel is broken.

item.title: Resolve 'Element Not Clickable' Errors in Selenium WebDriver
item.description:
“Resolve ‘Element Not Clickable’ Errors in Selenium WebDriver”

Encountering the “Element … is not clickable at point (x, y). Other element would receive the click” exception in Selenium WebDriver can halt your automated tests. This common issue arises from various factors that prevent the intended element from receiving the click event. Understanding these causes is the first step toward resolving them.

The core of this problem lies in the dynamic nature of web pages. Elements might be present in the Document Object Model (DOM) but not yet visible, interactable, or are obscured by other elements at the moment your script attempts to interact with them. Let’s explore the typical scenarios and their remedies.
